title: DeLand football completes season-long run as Volusia-Flagler unanimous No. 1 in final poll - NewsBreak
text:
By Zach Allen ,
1 days ago
Editor's note: News-Journal power rankings are determined by the votes of sportswriters Zach Allen, Chris Boyle and Chris Vinel. A first-place vote is worth five points, second place is worth four points and so on.
The top-five Volusia-Flagler football programs are officially solidified.
The power rankings remain unchanged following the regular season's finale in Week 11 . And spoiler alert: That probably won't change with a limited amount of local programs seeing action during the designated makeup week before the postseason begins.
Three top-five local teams picked up wins in Week 11, another saw its game canceled due to weather, and the last put up a fight against a higher-ranked team in an annual rivalry game .
Here's the final set of power rankings for the 2026 football season.
5. Flagler Palm Coast (three points)
Flagler Palm Coast completed its bounce-back season with an emphatic 63-18 rout over Orange Park on Oct. 30.
The Bulldogs went 3-7 in the first season under head coach Patrick Turner in 2025, but they completely flipped the script in 2026. Flagler Palm Coast cruised to an 8-2 season with multiple comfortable victories, and running back Ehimen Ajede had a breakout year with 1,767 rushing yards and 20 touchdowns.
The Bulldogs had a couple of slips against Tocoi Creek and Creekside, which prevented them from winning their district and probably making the playoffs. However, it doesn't take away from the fact that Flagler Palm Coast was one of the best in the Volusia-Flagler area this year.
4. Seabreeze (six points)
Seabreeze lost its 16th consecutive game to Daytona Beach rival Mainland, but it was a much closer game than the state MaxPreps rankings predicted it to be.
The Buccaneers defeated the Sandcrabs 6-0 in a defensive clash at Daytona Stadium. Seabreeze, ranked No. 228 in Florida, had chances to topple the No. 39-ranked Buccaneers, but it fell just short.
The loss keeps the Sandcrabs comfortably at No. 4 because it proved they could hang with the upper echelon of Volusia-Flagler football. The MaxPreps rankings seem to agree, as Seabreeze currently retains its No. 8 seeding in the Region 2-4A bracket.
3. Spruce Creek (nine points)
Spruce Creek remains at No. 3 after weather got in the way of its regular-season finale.
The Hawks were set to travel south to Fort Pierce to play John Carroll Catholic in a top-100 battle, but the threat of rain canceled the affair before it began.
As a result, Spruce Creek finished its regular season with a 5-4 record and will likely be playing postseason football once again.
2. Mainland (12 points)
The Buccaneers are still at No. 2 despite their close game with Seabreeze. A win is a win, especially in a rivalry game against a team fighting for a playoff spot.
Friday night's clash was the first start for sophomore quarterback Cailan James, who made his debut a week prior against DeLand after PJ Miller was injured on the team's opening drive. James completed 12 of 20 passes for 112 yards.
The victory improved Mainland to 5-4 ahead of its 33rd consecutive playoff appearance. The Bucs are currently slated as the No. 3 seed in Region 1-6A.
1. DeLand (15 points)
DeLand was the unanimous No. 1 in our preseason rankings, and a 9-1 season saw the Bulldogs keep their status from beginning to end.
DeLand's latest triumph was a 44-13 victory over Spanish River. It would be considered an explosive offensive performance by any other team's standards, but the Bulldogs' 44 points were actually their lowest since beating Spruce Creek 42-14 on Sept. 25.
That's just how good DeLand has been this season.
The Bulldogs are currently the No. 2 seed in Region 1-6A behind Seminole. But don't be fooled, DeLand is a serious contender for a Class 6A state title.
This article originally appeared on The Daytona Beach News-Journal: DeLand football completes season-long run as Volusia-Flagler unanimous No. 1 in final poll
